slides.title: Definition
slides.rawText: Artificial Intelligence Definition The broadest concept — any technique that enables computers to mimic human intelligence Key Characteristic Can be rule-based, symbolic, or learning-based systems Goal Simulate human cognitive functions like reasoning, problem-solving, perception Examples Chess-playing programs Expert systems Speech recognition Robot navigation

slides.title: Definition
slides.rawText: Machine Learning (Subset of AI) Definition AI systems that learn from data without being explicitly programmed for every rule Key Characteristic Uses statistical algorithms to find patterns and improve with experience Approach Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning Examples Email spam filters Recommendation systems Fraud detection Price prediction

Definition

AI systems that learn from data without being explicitly programmed for every rule

Key Characteristic

Uses statistical algorithms to find patterns and improve with experience

Approach

Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning

Examples

Email spam filters Recommendation systems Fraud detection Price prediction

slides.title: Definition
slides.rawText: Deep Learning (Subset of ML) Definition ML using multi-layered neural networks to learn complex representations from data Key Characteristic Neural networks with 3+ layers that automatically extract features Power Excels with unstructured data: images, audio, text, video Examples Image recognition Natural language processing Self-driving cars Voice assistants

Deep Learning (Subset of ML)

Definition

ML using multi-layered neural networks to learn complex representations from data

Key Characteristic

Neural networks with 3+ layers that automatically extract features

Power

Excels with unstructured data: images, audio, text, video

Examples

Image recognition Natural language processing Self-driving cars Voice assistants

slides.title: Slide 5
slides.rawText: The Hierarchy Relationship AI ML DL AI - Broadest Concept ML - Subset of AI DL - Subset of ML AI All DL is ML All ML is AI ML All DL is ML Not all ML is DL DL Specialized ML Neural networks

slides.title: Slide 6
slides.rawText: Key Differences At A Glance Aspect AI ML DL Scope Broadest - any intelligent system Subset - learns from data Subset - neural networks Data Need Can work without data (rule-based) Requires data for training Needs massive amounts of data Human Intervention High (explicit programming) Medium (feature engineering) Low (automatic feature extraction) Best For Simple, rule-based tasks Structured data, predictions Unstructured data, complex patterns Hardware Standard CPU CPU or GPU GPU/TPU required Choose based on problem complexity and data availability

slides.title: AI = The Umbrella
slides.rawText: Summary: The Big Picture AI = The Umbrella Any technique enabling machines to mimic human intelligence ML = Learning from Data AI that improves through experience without explicit programming DL = Neural Networks ML using deep neural networks for complex pattern recognition All Deep Learning is Machine Learning All Machine Learning is AI But not all AI is Machine Learning, and not all ML is Deep Learning

Summary: The Big Picture

AI = The Umbrella

Any technique enabling machines to mimic human intelligence

ML = Learning from Data

AI that improves through experience without explicit programming

DL = Neural Networks

ML using deep neural networks for complex pattern recognition

All Deep Learning is Machine Learning

All Machine Learning is AI

But not all AI is Machine Learning, and not all ML is Deep Learning

); }; export default Slide7_Summary;
